segments.text: - Hi, I'm Parker Mertz. I'm the manager of the Consumer Action Division. Individuals contact our office all the time reporting scams. And today we're gonna go over a scam that was sent via text message and see if we can spot some of the tells. This was a scam that was received via text message

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: claimed to be from Apple regarding a transaction made on an individual's account. The text looks very official, provides an Apple ID case number, provides a date and time when this allegedly illicit transaction happened. On the text message, they list a phone number and an address

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: to a link to click that looks very official and looks like it might be affiliated with Apple. This one is very well put together. You'll notice that the language in a lot of text messages and a lot of scams can be a telltale sign, but with AI progressing and becoming part of our everyday lives, there's nothing in the language that immediately jumps out as an issue.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: in this case i actually had to go to apple's website and check and i found that this link provided here is not actually affiliated in any way with apple additionally i checked on apple's website for its general customer service phone number it was not listed on the website and in fact had been flagged on some scam reporting type websites so if you receive a text message like

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: would advise first thing, don't click any links on your phone and don't call any phone numbers that are provided to you. Go directly to the Apple website, log into your account, see if there's any information on the account that would be related to a transaction that you don't recognize. If you do click the link or do call the number and give out any information or make a payment in some way, we would encourage you to report everything you can to

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: www.ic3.gov, the Internet Crime Complaint Center, who is affiliated with the Federal Bureau of Investigation and several other law enforcement agencies in the United States and worldwide. Additionally, if you get a scam text that you're not sure of, you can always feel free to contact the Minnesota Attorney General's office. You can be reached at 651-296-3353 to explain the problem, and a real live person will talk to you and get you the best advice that we can.
